section.sectionSummaryBrief: This explains that the engagement in Torah and mitzvos of one Jew empowers even those captive to their evil inclination, because all Jews, including the wicked, share a single essence through the hidden point of fear of Heaven.
section.t: And it can be said that this is also the reason for this, that the engagement in Torah and mitzvos of one gives strength and power
(not only to those who are in a place of decree,
but)
also to those who are captive in the hands of their evil inclination,
to redeem them from captivity
(as above in section 2),
because in each and every Jew,
even in the wicked,
there is
(at least in concealment)
the point of fear of Heaven,
and therefore all the categories of Israel
(righteous, intermediate, and wicked)
are one reality.
And as is hinted also in the word "tzibbur"
(that Israel are a tzibbur48),
"tzibbur" is an acronym for tzaddikim, beinonim, and resha'im49,
that all these three types are one reality
[And the vav
(that is in the word "tzibbur")
is the vav that connects the wicked with the intermediate and the righteous,
and even the head of the entire word is the letter tzaddik,
and Your people50
are all righteous].
And therefore the engagement in Torah and mitzvos of the righteous and the intermediate
[and especially when their engagement in Torah and mitzvos is in a manner that they include themselves with all of Israel51,
"Love your fellow as yourself"52]
also affects those who are captive in the hands of their evil inclination,
that they will go out from captivity and become righteous
(also openly).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This extends the principle that the unity of Israel allows the mitzvos performed by Jews in the Land to benefit those in exile, and those performed in the Temple era to benefit later generations.
section.t: And behold, the above matter
(that the engagement in Torah and mitzvos of one gives strength and power also to another)
applies not only when the coercion
(regarding some mitzvah)
is due to a decree of the kingdom or because his evil inclination overpowered him,
but also when the coercion is because according to Torah it is impossible to fulfill this mitzvah,
like Jews who are in the diaspora, for whom according to Torah it is impossible to fulfill the mitzvos dependent on the Land,
and similarly in the totality of the time of exile, when it is impossible
(even for the children of Israel who are in the Land of Israel)
to fulfill the mitzvos dependent on the time when the Holy Temple existed,
behold, from the aspect that all Israel in all places and in all times are one reality,
therefore, through the fact that the children of Israel who are in the Land of Israel fulfill the mitzvos dependent on the Land,
this also benefits the children of Israel who are in the diaspora,
and similarly regarding the mitzvos dependent on the time of the Temple that Israel fulfilled then,
this also benefits the children of Israel in the time of exile,
since all Israel throughout all the generations are one tzibbur, for there is no death for a tzibbur53
[therefore the sacrifice that was offered in the days of Ezra also atoned for the Israel who were in the generation of Tzidkiyahu54].

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This explains that the dispersion of Israel among the nations is a "righteousness" that leads to the future expansion of Jerusalem, achieved through the current service of mesirus nefesh and the spreading of the wellsprings outward.
section.t: And this is "the righteousness of His nobles in Israel, charity..." that He scattered them among the nations,
for that which it says "perazono"
(and not "pizrono")
is,
because the charity that the Holy One, blessed be He, did with Israel in scattering them among the nations is that through this they will in the future come to "open villages shall Jerusalem dwell"
(as explained above at length).
And another reason for that which it says "perazono" is,
because in order to come to "open villages shall Jerusalem dwell" it is through that also the service in the time of exile
(when He scattered them among the nations)
is in a manner of "open villages shall Jerusalem dwell."
For in addition to this that the entry into Jerusalem in the physical sense,
in the true redemption through our righteous Moshiach,
is through the service of Jerusalem,
the perfection of fear
[for the coming of Moshiach will be through "in His voice you shall listen"55,
that this
(the matter of "in His voice you shall listen")
is through fear,
which is the beginning of service and its essence and root56,
for although in order for the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos to be complete, love is also needed57,
nevertheless, the essence of service is fear58],
behold, in order that there be "open villages shall Jerusalem dwell,"
the service must be even now in a manner of "open villages,"
above measure and limitation,
which in general is the service of mesirus nefesh,
surrender of the will59,
and this service is a close preparation that there will be "open villages shall Jerusalem dwell" also in its simple sense,
"In the future Jerusalem will spread out over all the Land of Israel, and in the future the Land of Israel will spread out over all the lands."
And this is accomplished
(like all the matters of the future60)
through our deeds and our service during the time of exile,
the totality of which are the three lines of Torah, service, and acts of kindness
[and as our sages, of blessed memory, said in Tractate Berachos at its beginning and outset61
on the verse62
"He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, for many were with me,"
"Whoever engages in Torah and acts of kindness and prays with the tzibbur, I consider it as if he redeemed Me and My children from among the nations of the world"],
and especially through the service of "spread forth your wellsprings outward," through which "the master, King Moshiach, will come"
[as stated in the letter of the Baal Shem Tov63
what he heard in the palace of Moshiach,
"from the King Moshiach"].
